newsitem.title: USA: MILLSTONE 3 COST RECOVERY SOUGHT FROM NU.
newsitem.headline: MILLSTONE 3 COST RECOVERY SOUGHT FROM NU.

text.p: The nine non-operating owners of the Millstone 3 nuclear power facility have filed a demand arbitration and lawsuits seeking to recover losses associated with the shutdown of the power plant, lawyers for the companies said Thursday.
They said the non-operating owners conservatively estimate their costs for replacement power and operation and maintenance resulting from the shutdown will exceed $200 million.
The nine have a 19.5 percent interest in the 1,154 megawatt nuclear reactor, the lawyers noted in a statement.

It said the nine non-operators filed a demand for arbitration with Connecticut Light and Power Co and Western Massachusetts Electric Co as well as lawsuits against Northeast Utilities and its trustees in Massachusetts.
The two utilities are Northeast Utilities subsidiaries that have a 65 percent interest in Millstone 3, one of three nuclear power plants located at Millstone Station in Waterford, Conn.

The non-operating owners claim that Northeast Utilities and its subsidiaries failed to comply with Nuclear Regulatory Commission regulations, failed to operate the facility in accordance with good utility operating practice and attempted to conceal their activities from the non-operating owners and the NRC.

"Northeast Utilities' senior management purposefully engaged in an arrogant game of brinkmanship with the NRC to save money and free up cash and deservedly lost. The real tragedy is that innocent utilities and their customers and shareholders have paid an enormous price for someone else's deliberate wrongdoing," said Shaun Sullivan, the lead attorney for the non-operating owners.
The non-operating owners paid Northeast Utilities to operate the plant in exchange for power, he explained.

On June 25, 1996, he noted, the NRC concluded safety problems at Millstone 3 were so pervasive that it ordered NU to obtain full commission approval prior to restarting the unit and downgraded the plant to a Category 3 status -- the category reserved for the worst nuclear plants in the United States. The Millstone facilities are the first plants in the nation to be given a Category 3 status since 1987.
